findings: ACCEPTANCE-COMMAND GUARD HOLE (highest value, from PANELFONT-M3). pytest tests -k panel, the exact command both the receipt and the audit cite as acceptance-4 evidence, deselects tests/test_rope_design_conformance.py::test_no_hardcoded_hex_or_px_outside_designsystem. A QWidget subclass carrying a hardcoded hex AND a hardcoded px, appended to synapse_panel.py, passes that command with 352 green. The guard itself is healthy and reddens the instant it is actually run. The remedy is the command, not new code: select by path, not by the substring 'panel'. This outlives this leg - every panel leg using -k panel as its gate inherits the hole.

THE FLOOR IS A RATCHET, NOT YET A MEASUREMENT. FONT_FLOOR_PX = 10 is defined AS the smallest size already shipped (SIZE_MICRO), so 'no size token below the floor' could not have failed on the day it was written. It is a real anti-regression ratchet (M2 proves it bites, and it is the only guard that does) but it is not yet what Joe's law asks for - 'no smaller than the Houdini default'. That stays UNKNOWN until the GUI probe is pasted. The builder states this in the token comment, audit section 4, the receipt, and the BP4-FLOOR-LIFT spawn. Nothing is papered over; the leg is correctly SOUND-WITH-NITS at best, never SOUND.

THE DOC-STATED SEARCH REPRODUCES, AND WIDER. The crux searched the entire H22.0.400 help cache (2280 files), not the builder's ref+basics+hom subset. Exactly one file matches 'UI font|default font|font size|fontsize|interface font' and it is the third-party MOPs Plus Typography SOP's own Font Size PARAMETER doc. Zero files match preference-flavoured phrasings. The UNKNOWN provenance is honest.

THE AUDIT'S INVENTORY IS EXACT, NOT ROUNDED. 167 / 88 / 33 / 13 reproduce to the digit under bare-word occurrence counting over python/synapse/panel/**/*.py including tokens.py. Under a stricter line-with-colon method excluding tokens.py the numbers are 164 / 87 / 33 / 7; the deltas are entirely method, chiefly 6 prose mentions of line-height inside comments explaining that Qt does not implement it. No inflation.

THE DESIGN-SYSTEM AUTHORITY IS CLEANER THAN THE TEST PROVES. All 8 modules under designsystem/ score 0 under the test's own literal regex, but the test opens only qss.py. Widening the read to walk the designsystem package costs one loop, pins what is already true, and would then catch a literal introduced into components.py or fontload.py - which today nothing catches.

PANEL-WIDE, 166 TRULY HARDCODED TYPOGRAPHY LITERALS REMAIN OUTSIDE designsystem/, across 22 modules (styles.py 44, hda_views.py 33, context_bar.py 14, gate_widget.py 13, render_preflight.py 9, and 17 more). A further 8 hits are %-interpolated token feeds (font-size: %dpx filled from t.scaled(...)) and are NOT hardcoded - the test's regex whitelists brace interpolation only, so a crux that reported 174 without splitting would have overcounted by 8. These 166 are inventoried and spawned, not fixed; whether that satisfies acceptance 2 is a scope ruling, not an honesty question.

THE WEIGHT GUARD IS VALUE-BASED, NOT SOURCE-BASED (M4 vs M4b). It catches a weight outside 400/500/600 and misses a bare literal that equals a token. Semantically harmless today. The gap is between the test and its own docstring's 'never bare literals' claim.

COSMETIC: the qss literal test reports line numbers computed on the comment-stripped body, so PANELFONT-M1 at source line 51 was reported as L42. Anyone chasing the offender lands in the wrong rule block.

THE 5-SCALE HASH CLAIM IS REAL AND SENSITIVE. Branch == master == the builder's five hashes at all five scales, and both mutations that touched a rendered value moved all five. The byte-identical claim is a measurement, not a hash that cannot move.

THE DIFF IS GENUINELY SUBSTITUTION-ONLY. Zero new import/def/class/QTimer/connect(/QWidget/Signal/Slot in the added lines of qss.py and tokens.py; the synapse_panel.py diff is 0 bytes against base. No behaviour surface was opened.
lane_verdict: SOUND-WITH-NITS. Every headless acceptance row reproduces independently and the gui_required row is correctly declared UNKNOWN. Two mutations reddened as designed, one survived on a guard nuance whose control proves the guard alive, and one exposed a hole in the ACCEPTANCE COMMAND rather than in the code. The single substantive open question is a scope ruling on acceptance 2, which the builder itself routed to the referee.
